title: Covariant stationary Noether charge and Wald entropy

items.title: Stationary covariant Noether boundary data
items.design_state: Step 1 carrier authored for batch 117; local support item added only where needed to prove the planned stationary Noether-charge result.
items.physical_scope: Smooth classical diffeomorphism-covariant metric field theories with a specified finite-jet Lagrangian, stationary nondegenerate bifurcate horizon, globally compatible Noether charge, and explicitly integrable asymptotic Hamiltonian boundary data. It does not adopt a quantum model or identify Noether-charge entropy with thermodynamic entropy.
items.statement:
Let $n\ge2$, let $M$ be an oriented, time-oriented smooth $n$-manifold, and let $g$ be a smooth Lorentzian metric of signature $(-,+,\ldots,+)$. Write $\boldsymbol\epsilon_g$ for its oriented metric volume form. Let $\nabla$ be its Levi-Civita connection, the unique torsion-free, metric-compatible connection. Let $\phi=(g,\psi)$ denote a smooth section of a specified field bundle $\pi:E\to M$, including the metric and any other dynamical fields $\psi$ that are smooth tensor fields with the pullback action of spacetime diffeomorphisms. An admitted field family is a smooth map $\Phi:P\times M\to E$ with $\pi(\Phi(p,x))=x$, where $P$ is a finite-dimensional smooth parameter manifold; for $v\in T_pP$, $\delta_v\phi$ is the derivative of $\Phi$ along any smooth parameter curve with initial velocity $v$. A **finite-jet Lagrangian $n$-form** is a smooth spacetime $n$-form $\mathcal L(\phi)$ whose coordinate coefficients depend smoothly on the field components and finitely many spacetime derivatives. It is **diffeomorphism-covariant** when pullback by every admitted local diffeomorphism $\Psi$ satisfies $\mathcal L(\Psi^*\phi)=\Psi^*\mathcal L(\phi)$.

A **chosen covariant first-variation decomposition** is data consisting of an Euler–Lagrange expression $E_\phi[\eta]$, the $n$-form linear in a field variation $\eta$ left after spacetime derivatives have been moved off $\eta$ by integration by parts, and a covariant $(n-1)$-form $\theta(\phi;\eta)$, also linear in $\eta$, such that
$$\delta\mathcal L=E_\phi[\delta\phi]+d\theta(\phi;\delta\phi)$$
for every admitted smooth finite-dimensional family of fields. Here covariance means that for every admitted local diffeomorphism $\Psi$ and field variation $\eta$,
$$E_{\Psi^*\phi}[\Psi^*\eta]=\Psi^*E_\phi[\eta],\qquad \theta(\Psi^*\phi;\Psi^*\eta)=\Psi^*\theta(\phi;\eta).$$
The choice of $\theta$ is part of the data and need not be unique. A solution has $E_\phi=0$; a linearized solution $\delta\phi$ at $\phi$ has $\delta E_\phi[\delta\phi]=0$.

A smooth embedded submanifold is **spacelike** when its induced metric is positive definite. A smooth embedded codimension-one submanifold $N\subset M$ is a **null hypersurface** when the pullback metric $g|_{TN}$ is degenerate with a one-dimensional kernel; that kernel is the null line distribution tangent and normal to $N$.

A **stationary solution with generator $\xi$** is a solution $\phi$ and a fixed smooth spacetime vector field $\xi$ such that $\mathcal L_\xi\phi=0$. Thus $\mathcal L_\xi g=0$, so $\xi$ is a Killing field of $g$. A **bifurcate Killing horizon** is a pair of smooth embedded null hypersurfaces $N_+$ and $N_-$, each invariant under the local flow of $\xi$, meeting transversely in a compact codimension-two submanifold $B$, such that away from $B$ the nonzero field $\xi$ spans the null line distribution of each hypersurface and $\xi=0$ on $B$. Fix $B$ to be oriented, boundaryless, and spacelike. Choose a future-directed unit timelike normal $u$ and a chosen unit spacelike normal $n_B$ along $B$, orthogonal to each other, and define the binormal $\epsilon_{ab}=2u_{[a}(n_B)_{b]}$, so $\epsilon_{ab}\epsilon^{ab}=-2$. Orient $B$ compatibly with the spacetime orientation and this normal frame so that, on $B$, $(\boldsymbol\epsilon_g)_{ab a_3\ldots a_n}=\epsilon_{ab}(dA_B)_{a_3\ldots a_n}$; here $dA_B$ is the positive volume form of the induced metric with that orientation. The horizon is **nondegenerate** when the fixed normalization of $\xi$ gives a constant $\kappa>0$ on $B$ with $\nabla_a\xi_b=\kappa\epsilon_{ab}$ there; $\kappa$ is its surface gravity. Variations keep $\xi$ and the embedded surface $B$ fixed.

For such data define the **Noether current** $(n-1)$-form
$$J_\xi:=\theta(\phi;\mathcal L_\xi\phi)-\iota_\xi\mathcal L.$$
Choose a smooth covariant $(n-2)$-form $Q_\xi$ on a neighborhood of the admitted field data and define the residual constraint form $C_\xi:=J_\xi-dQ_\xi$. Require $C_\xi=0$ on the selected solution and, for each admitted linearized perturbation used below, require its fixed-$\xi$ variation $\delta C_\xi=0$. These are explicit on-shell and linearized-constraint conditions; no existence or global exactness of $Q_\xi$ follows merely from closure of a presymplectic current. The pullback of $Q_\xi$ is required to be globally compatible on the integration region.

Here a **smooth solution space** $\mathcal S$ is a specified smooth manifold whose points are the admitted smooth solution fields satisfying the chosen boundary falloff. A smooth curve in $\mathcal S$ is viewed as a family of sections of $E$; its tangent vector $v\in T_\phi\mathcal S$ induces a field variation $\delta_v\phi$. Every admitted perturbation used in the constraint-variation and boundary-charge statements below is such a tangent variation, and $d_{\mathcal S}H_\xi$ acts on these tangent vectors.

Boundary data also include a family of closed codimension-two surfaces $S_R$ approaching the asymptotic boundary, and finite oriented smooth singular hypersurface chains $C_R$ with $\partial C_R=S_R-B$. With a fixed boundary-term convention, define the charge-variation one-form by
$$\alpha_\xi(\delta\phi):=\lim_{R\to\infty}\int_{S_R}\bigl(\delta Q_\xi-\iota_\xi\theta(\phi;\delta\phi)\bigr).$$
Require this limit to exist and be globally integrable: there is a smooth Hamiltonian charge $H_\xi$ on the specified solution space with $d_{\mathcal S}H_\xi=\alpha_\xi$, where $d_{\mathcal S}$ is the exterior derivative on that solution space. This exactness, and the chosen boundary formula itself, are hypotheses. Other boundary actions or falloff conditions can add terms and require a separately stated charge formula.

Adopt the $c=1$ action-unit convention: time is measured as length, $[\hbar]=\text{action}$, and $[k_B]=\text{energy}/\text{temperature}$; neither $\hbar$ nor $k_B$ is set to $1$. Normalize the flow parameter of the fixed generator $\xi$ in length units. Then its Lie action and $\nabla\xi$ have units $L^{-1}$, and the surface gravity $\kappa$ in $\nabla_a\xi_b=\kappa\epsilon_{ab}$ has units $L^{-1}$. The spacetime integral of $\mathcal L$ has units of action, so if $\mathcal L=\ell\boldsymbol\epsilon_g$, then $[\ell]=\text{action}\,L^{-n}$. Since curvature has units $L^{-2}$, the Einstein--Hilbert normalization $\ell_{\rm EH}=R/(16\pi G)$ in $n$ spacetime dimensions has $[G]=L^{n-2}\,\text{action}^{-1}$. Thus the curvature derivative $P^{abcd}$ used below has units $[P]=\text{action}\,L^{2-n}$, and the downstream functional $-(2\pi k_B/\hbar)\int_B P^{abcd}\epsilon_{ab}\epsilon_{cd}\,dA_B$ has entropy units $k_B$. The integrated Noether charge and $H_\xi$ have energy units, consistent with $\hbar\kappa\,\delta S_W/k_B$.

When SI units are restored for the $n$-dimensional Einstein--Hilbert normalization $c^3R/(16\pi G)$, $[G]={\rm m}^{n-1}{\rm kg}^{-1}{\rm s}^{-2}$ and $[A_B]={\rm m}^{n-2}$, so the area expression is $S_W=k_Bc^3A_B/(4G\hbar)$. In four spacetime dimensions this is the usual SI Newton constant in ${\rm m}^3{\rm kg}^{-1}{\rm s}^{-2}$ and horizon area in ${\rm m}^2$; the SI acceleration surface gravity is $\kappa_{\rm acc}=c^2\kappa_{\rm geom}$.

references.title: Vivek Iyer and Robert M. Wald, Some Properties of Noether Charge and a Proposal for Dynamical Black Hole Entropy, §§2–4
Geoffrey Compère and Adrien Fiorucci, Advanced Lectures on General Relativity, §§1.3.1–1.3.3 and §1.4.2
Daniel Harlow and Jie-qiang Wu, Covariant phase space with boundaries, §§2.2–2.4

items.title: Noether charge decomposition for algebraic-curvature Lagrangians
items.design_state: Step 1 carrier authored for batch 117; local support item added only where needed to prove the planned stationary Noether-charge result.
items.physical_scope: Local covariant Noether-potential decomposition for smooth classical metric theories with finite covariant matter jets and algebraic dependence on curvature. The result fixes the derivative-of-generator coefficient in the canonical local charge representative; it is not an entropy law or a thermodynamic identification.
items.statement:
Use the metric, tensor fields, covariant first-variation decomposition, and
Noether current of the preceding Definition. Suppose the Lagrangian is
$$\mathcal L=\ell(g_{ab},R_{abcd},\psi,\nabla\psi,\ldots,\nabla_{(a_1}\cdots\nabla_{a_m)}\psi)\,\boldsymbol\epsilon_g,$$
where $m<\infty$, all fields and coefficients are smooth, and the curvature
argument is algebraic (there are no covariant derivatives of $R_{abcd}$).
Use the curvature convention
$$R(X,Y)Z=\nabla_X\nabla_YZ-\nabla_Y\nabla_XZ-\nabla_{[X,Y]}Z,$$
and write $R_{abcd}:=g(R(e_c,e_d)e_b,e_a)$ in any local frame. Square
brackets denote weight-one antisymmetrization.
Define the Riemann-symmetric derivative $P^{abcd}$ by
$$\delta\ell\big|_{g,\psi,\nabla\psi,\ldots}=P^{abcd}\delta R_{abcd},$$
with $P^{abcd}=-P^{bacd}=-P^{abdc}=P^{cdab}$ and $P^{a[bcd]}=0$.

Use the covariant first-variation potential produced by the finite covariant
integration-by-parts construction on the field jets, up to the stated
potential ambiguities. For each smooth vector field $\zeta$, use the local
Noether potential obtained by covariantly integrating the derivatives of
$\zeta$ in $J_\zeta=\theta(\phi;\mathcal L_\zeta\phi)-\iota_\zeta\mathcal L$
by parts.
Call this the **canonical local representative**: it is defined on a
neighborhood of the fields and generators, is a local covariant primitive of
$J_\zeta$ on shell, and has no independent closed-form addition. The permitted
representative changes are exactly those induced by
$$\mathcal L\mapsto\mathcal L+d\mu,\qquad \theta\mapsto\theta+\delta\mu+d\mathbf Y,$$
and by an exact charge change; here $\mu$ is a covariant $(n-1)$-form and
$\mathbf Y(\phi;\eta)$ is a covariant $(n-2)$-form linear in $\eta$.
Assume the chosen representative is globally compatible on the integration
region. Then it has the form
$$Q_\zeta=W^c\zeta_c+X^{cd}\nabla_{[c}\zeta_{d]} +\mathbf Y(\phi;\mathcal L_\zeta\phi)+dZ,$$
where $W^c$ and $X^{cd}$ are local covariant form-valued coefficients,
$Z$ is a local covariant $(n-3)$-form (the exact term is absent when $n=2$),
and
$$(X^{cd})_{a_3\ldots a_n} =-P^{abcd}(\boldsymbol\epsilon_g)_{ab a_3\ldots a_n}.$$
For the canonical representative before the permitted changes one may take
$\mathbf Y=0$ and $Z=0$.

Geoffrey Compère and Adrien Fiorucci, Advanced Lectures on General Relativity, §§1.3.1–1.3.3
Daniel Harlow and Jie-qiang Wu, Covariant phase space with boundaries, §§2.2–2.4

items.title: Stationary horizon Noether-charge entropy variation
items.design_state: Step 1 carrier authored for batch 117; local support item added only where needed to prove the planned stationary Noether-charge result.
items.physical_scope: Classical stationary nondegenerate bifurcate horizons in smooth diffeomorphism-covariant metric theories whose Lagrangian depends algebraically on curvature and has no covariant derivatives of curvature. The result is a conditional Noether-charge identity, not a dynamical second law or an empirical or quantum statement.
items.statement:
Use the stationary Noether data of the preceding Definition, with fixed $\xi$, compact boundaryless bifurcation surface $B$, and surface gravity $\kappa>0$. Choose the covariant first-variation potential and $Q_\xi$ in the canonical local representative class of the preceding Noether-charge decomposition theorem. Let $\nabla$ be the Levi-Civita connection of $g$, use the curvature convention
$$R(X,Y)Z=\nabla_X\nabla_YZ-\nabla_Y\nabla_XZ-\nabla_{[X,Y]}Z,$$
and write $R_{abcd}:=g(R(e_c,e_d)e_b,e_a)$ in any local frame and $R:=g^{ac}g^{bd}R_{abcd}$. Write $\mathcal L=\ell(g,\psi,\nabla\psi,\ldots,R)\,\boldsymbol\epsilon_g$, where $\boldsymbol\epsilon_g$ is the oriented metric volume form and $\ell$ depends smoothly on the Riemann tensor algebraically, with no covariant derivatives of $R$. Define $P^{abcd}$ to be the Riemann-symmetric metric representative of the differential of $\ell$ in its curvature argument:
$$\delta\ell\big|_{g,\psi,\nabla\psi,\ldots}=P^{abcd}\delta R_{abcd}.$$
Here $P$ satisfies $P^{abcd}=-P^{bacd}=-P^{abdc}=P^{cdab}$ and $P^{a[bcd]}=0$. Let $dA_B$ be the positive volume form of the induced Riemannian metric on $B$ (in local coordinates with induced metric $h$, $dA_B=\sqrt{\det h}\,dy^1\cdots dy^{n-2}$), and define the stationary Wald Noether-charge functional
$$S_W:=-\frac{2\pi k_B}{\hbar}\int_B P^{abcd}\epsilon_{ab}\epsilon_{cd}\,dA_B.$$
For every admitted smooth linearized perturbation at the stationary solution, with $\xi$ and $B$ fixed and the residual constraint variation $\delta C_\xi=0$, the chosen Noether charge satisfies
$$\delta\int_B Q_\xi=\frac{\hbar\kappa}{2\pi k_B}\,\delta S_W.$$
Here $\hbar>0$ is Planck's constant, $k_B>0$ is Boltzmann's constant, and the action normalization is $c=1$. The identity is evaluated at the unperturbed value of $\kappa$; it does not include a $\delta\kappa$ term.

references.title: Vivek Iyer and Robert M. Wald, Some Properties of Noether Charge and a Proposal for Dynamical Black Hole Entropy, §§3–4, equations (38)–(60)
Geoffrey Compère and Adrien Fiorucci, Advanced Lectures on General Relativity, §§1.3.1–1.3.3
Daniel Harlow and Jie-qiang Wu, Covariant phase space with boundaries, §§2.2–2.4

items.title: Stationary first law from the covariant boundary identity
items.design_state: Step 1 carrier authored for batch 117; local support item added only where needed to prove the planned stationary Noether-charge result.
items.physical_scope: Conditional first law for a classical stationary nondegenerate bifurcate horizon with the specified covariant potential, globally compatible Noether charge, vanishing linearized constraint variation, and integrable asymptotic Hamiltonian charge. It is not a dynamical law, a quantum result, or empirical confirmation of a gravity model.
items.statement:
For the stationary Noether data of the preceding Definition, choose $Q_\xi$ in the canonical local representative class of the preceding Noether-charge decomposition theorem. Let $\delta\phi$ be an admitted linearized solution with fixed $\xi$ and $\delta C_\xi=0$. Let $C_R$ be finite oriented smooth singular hypersurface chains with $\partial C_R=S_R-B$, where the boundary orientations are outward at $S_R$ and inward at $B$. Then
$$d(\delta Q_\xi-\iota_\xi\theta)=0$$
on each $C_R$, and
$$\delta H_\xi=\lim_{R\to\infty}\int_{S_R}(\delta Q_\xi-\iota_\xi\theta) =\int_B\delta Q_\xi =\frac{\hbar\kappa}{2\pi k_B}\,\delta S_W.$$
The last equality uses the derivative-free curvature hypothesis and the Noether entropy functional of the preceding theorem. The identity is conditional on the exact boundary-charge and vanishing-constraint assumptions; $\kappa$ is the unperturbed surface gravity. For the Einstein-Hilbert Lagrangian $\mathcal L_{\rm EH}=R\boldsymbol\epsilon_g/(16\pi G)$ with Newton constant $G>0$ in the same $c=1$ action normalization, it gives $S_W=k_BA_B/(4G\hbar)$, where $A_B:=\int_B dA_B$.

references.title: Vivek Iyer and Robert M. Wald, Some Properties of Noether Charge and a Proposal for Dynamical Black Hole Entropy, §6, equations (73)–(102)
Geoffrey Compère and Adrien Fiorucci, Advanced Lectures on General Relativity, §§1.3.3–1.4.2
Daniel Harlow and Jie-qiang Wu, Covariant phase space with boundaries, §§2.2–2.4

title: Covariant stationary Noether charge and Wald entropy — Examples

items.title: f(R) stationary entropy coefficient
items.design_state: Step 1 carrier authored for batch 117; local support item added only where needed to prove the planned stationary Noether-charge result.
items.physical_scope: Classical f(R) metric Lagrangians on smooth stationary nondegenerate bifurcate horizons under the algebraic-curvature assumptions of the stationary Noether first law. This is not a dynamical entropy law.
items.statement:
In units with $c=1$, let $\mathcal L=f(R)\boldsymbol\epsilon_g/(16\pi G)$, where $G>0$ is the Newton coupling in the given $n$-dimensional action normalization, with units $L^{n-2}/\mathrm{action}$. Choose an open interval $J\subseteq\mathbb R$ and $f\in C^\infty(J)$, and admit only smooth background fields and finite-dimensional smooth field families for which $R_{\phi_p}(x)\in J$ for every parameter $p$ and spacetime point $x\in M$. Thus this composed Lagrangian is smooth throughout the spacetime and variation domain required by the preceding first-law theorem; regularity only at curvature values on $B$ is not assumed. The scalar curvature $R$ has units $L^{-2}$, so $f$ has those units and $f'(R)$ is dimensionless. Under the same smooth stationary horizon assumptions as the preceding theorem,
$$S_W=\frac{k_B}{4G\hbar}\int_B f'(R)\,dA_B.$$
The example computes the Noether-charge functional only; it asserts no monotonicity along a dynamical horizon.

references.title: Vivek Iyer and Robert M. Wald, Some Properties of Noether Charge and a Proposal for Dynamical Black Hole Entropy, §§4–6
Geoffrey Compère and Adrien Fiorucci, Advanced Lectures on General Relativity, §1.3.3
